units.translation: And she (the earth) brings forth for mortals flocks of sheep and the life-giving grain of Demeter.
Or she will bear a son mightier than his father.
We suffered pains at the hands of those who bore us.
And we pray always that other tributes of the land be born (thus Erfurdt for 'and overseers').
Of the mother who has now given birth to this light of kindly night.
For the impious deed begets more after it.
Ancient hubris loves to beget a new hubris among the evils of mortals.
May old murder no longer breed in the house.
Guard lest boldness give birth to fear.
Night loves to bring forth pain for the wise helmsman.
And from this gain another gain is born.
Hearing Aeschylus (fr. 306b) saying that virtues are born for mortals from toils.

in which sense Herodotus and Thucydides use τιμωρός [avenger]: see Thesaurus vol. 7 p. 2213.
